toolCallComparison.definition: Both sides are computed by .tmp/fh-39620264048-metrics.mjs from the frozen agent/best-agent-evidence.jsonl of each cell, calls de-duplicated by callId. hardRejections = admission refusals carrying a code (malformed-input, not-found, permission-denied, too-large, occurrence-mismatch, unknown-command, conflict). ranAndFailed = the process started and ended nonzero. shellMetacharArgs counts exec calls whose command is not sh/bash/zsh and whose argv names |, &&, >, $( or ;; `literal` applies that rule verbatim (a grep alternation's | also matches) and `operator` keeps only tokens that really are shell operators. repeatedCommand = args[0] equals the command. deliverable = the cell wrote or ran its own deliverable path.

transportSeconds.sourceManifestClaim: config/frontier-harness-repro-39557190033.json#knownRisks.providerTransport states six stalls for 2246 seconds. A recount of the same eight cells from their frozen evidence gives 8 stalls for 2368 seconds, and the manifest's own per-cell list (1912 + 49529 + 6329 + 120003 + 24201 + 593882 + 460173 + 1111585 ms) sums to 2367.6 seconds, so both the count and the total in that sentence disagree with the cells it describes; this outcome and the record quote the recount.
transportSeconds.method: sum of every model-failure entry's durationMs in each cell's evidence, which is the stalled model call only, not the wall clock it cost the cell

outcome.toolAdmissionVerdict: No. No cell's verdict was produced by tool admission: the 3 refusals in this batch are all correct (two `file`/`xxd` binaries absent from the frozen PATH in extract-elf, one write conflict in gcode-to-text) and each cell kept working afterwards, extract-elf with a different tool went on to pass; every failed cell either never wrote its deliverable (chess-best-move, code-from-image, gcode-to-text, largest-eigenval), wrote a wrong one (dna-insert, meriyah's single specification-gap case) or ran out of budget on real work (build-cython-ext). What does persist is a diagnostic-cost shape: shell operators passed as literal argv (8 real cases, all in meriyah) and a command name repeated into args[0] (2 cases, build-cython-ext) each burn one round with an error message that does not say the tool has no shell.
